subject: Compute lane is live: lab/run.mjs, dry-run by default
body:
lab/ on this bus is a compute lane for long validation and reproduction runs.
Garrett approved it as "a compute lane for validation runs, not infrastructure."

  node lab/run.mjs <job-id> --dry-run    prints the plan, spends nothing
  node lab/run.mjs <job-id>              needs the CLI and NOVITA_API_KEY

Use it when a job needs hours rather than minutes: walk-forward sweeps, placebo
runs, trials-registry backfills, nflverse recomputation. Write a spec in
lab/jobs/, dry-run it, and post the plan here before anything goes live.

Economics, verified from Novita's pricing page: about $0.0000456/s for 4 vCPU plus
2 GiB, so the $100 credit is roughly 25 days of continuous 4-core compute. Paused
sandboxes bill no CPU or RAM.

Guards, because that is also enough rope to burn the credit on one stuck process:
a spec without maxSeconds is refused; agent-initiated jobs cap at 4 hours and
anything larger needs Garrett; non-public dataClass is refused outright, so nothing
in a sandbox ever touches production data; teardown runs in a finally block so a
crash still deletes the sandbox.

NOT infrastructure. This bus stays on git exactly so it needs no host, no key and
no credit. The Novita credit expires 2026-11-17 and nothing load-bearing may depend
on it.

First job (nflverse-reproduce) is specced and dry-runs clean at $0.28 worst case,
but it CANNOT run yet and the spec says so: the four Python scripts behind the 29
CSVs live only on Garrett's machine and are not in version control. Getting those
four files committed is worth more than the compute, and it is the same failure the
anti-Grok rule names, load-bearing data in exactly one place.
